name: anger
quote: I can't believe he said that to me!
description: Strong negative feeling towards a person or thing caused by a perceived injury and with a desire to deter the undesired behavior.
perceptions: This person or thing has done something I strongly dislike.
It has threatened or damaged the body or reputation of myself or someone close to me.
A display of anger might prevent it from happening again.
A display of anger is an option that won't make the problem worse.

guidance.description: We all know what anger is, and we’ve all felt it: whether as a fleeting annoyance or as full-fledged rage. Anger is a completely normal, usually healthy, human emotion. But when it gets out of control and turns destructive, it can lead to problems—problems at work, in your personal relationships, and in the overall quality of your life.

comparisons.description: Fear can cause anger if someone or something has put your in a dangerous situation or your brain thinks anger is an appropriate response. But fear can happen without anger, and you can be angry without being afraid.
Annoyance is a mild anger - you want a distraction to stop, but any effort may not be worthwhile.
Frustration is the sense of being blocked on a desired outcome, which can lead to anger at whatever or whoever you blame for the failure.

variations.name: suppressed anger
variations.description: Strong negative feeling towards a person or thing caused by a perceived injury, but a recognition that a display of anger is likely to make the problem worse.
perceptions: This person or thing has done something I strongly dislike.
It has threatened or damaged my body or reputation.
A display of anger is likely to make the problem worse.

guidance.description: Anger is a natural human emotion, but when it goes unexpressed or is pushed down, it can start to create hidden challenges in our lives. Repressed anger doesn’t disappear; instead, it often shows up as physical tension, anxiety, mood swings, or self-doubt, affecting both your mental and physical health. Understanding what causes repressed anger and how it manifests can be the first step in bringing it to the surface.

commentaries.quote: Here are some ways repressed anger can affect us: Depression, Subjugation, Paranoia, Self-Righteousness, Passive-Aggressiveness.
commentaries.attribution: Imi Lo MA in Psychology Today

variations.name: fearful anger
variations.description: Strong negative feeling towards a person or thing caused by a perceived injury and a concern that it could repeat or get worse.
perceptions: This person or thing has done something I strongly dislike.
It has threatened or damaged the body or reputation of myself or someone close to me.
It's likely to keep happening or get worse if I don't do something.
A display of anger might prevent it from happening again.
A display of anger is an option that won't make the problem worse.

guidance.description: One of the links between [fear and anger] is that they often feel unpleasant and are a response to difficult situations. In addition, people who evoke fear or anger in others may be viewed negatively. It can be helpful to look at their psychological roots to understand these connections in further detail and know how to cope with painful emotions.

variations.name: argument
variations.description: Negative feelings from a back-and-forth conversation with someone trying to resolve a conflict about something.
perceptions: I disagree with what this person has done or wants to do.
I need to convince them to see things as I do.
examples: Shouting match about who left the door open so the dog could get out.
The endless yelling about any culture war topic.

guidance.description: We’ve said that the nature of argument is that you and another person are trying to change each other’s minds. Now of course, there is always the possibility that the other person in the exchange is not really interested in reasoning with you, but is really just out to intimidate you or lure you into a position where your honesty can be used against you for the benefit of an audience friendly to their views. Arguing can backfire when it ends in heightened aggression, misunderstanding, or a doubling down on bad reasoning.

comparisons.description: 'Arguing' is a form of 'debating', but with intuitive justification and heated emotions.

commentaries.quote: Anger is how we tell others that we seriously want them to change their behavior. It's a threatening signal that they should back off that behavior or there could be consequences.

It is easy to fly into a passion-anybody can do that-but to be angry with the right person to the right extent and at the right time and with the right object and in the right way-that is not easy, and it is not everyone who can do it.
Speak when you are angry and you will make the best speech you will ever regret.
Do not teach your children never to be angry; teach them how to be angry.
Love implies anger. The man who is angered by nothing cares about nothing.
